tasks.short: Keep databases of known test defects.

steps.what: Create databases of known defects from the tracker.
Mark which defects are known and still current.
Maintain the databases from that mark.

tasks.design: Known defects load from {PROJECT} into {DATA_PLATFORM}. The tester marks which are still known and current. The database is maintained from that mark, not from every closed row.
tasks.previous_blocker: The known set was a spreadsheet that drifted from the tracker.
tasks.enabler_now: A tracker id and a status are fields. Whether a closed defect is still a known risk is not.
tasks.still_hard: A defect that was closed but will return stays a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The tester remembers which old defect the new failure resembles.
tasks.altitude: Loading and filing take less copying. Marking what is still known stays.

reach.task: Check a failure against the known set
reach.learn: Which defects the tester still calls known

evidence.claim: Loading tracker rows into a database is a copy. Deciding that a defect is still known is not.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the tester maintains the known set. Filing a new defect is a different task.
Structured input: defect id, status, area, build closed. Producer is the tracker. A row with no defect id is not loaded.
The mark is remaining time. Maintenance does not invent a defect.
unknowns: Does the tracker have a stable defect id?
Who else may call a defect known?
research_questions: How often is a known defect missing from the list?

already_counted.description: Marking known defects is already the remaining time on that step.

incremental.description: Drop defects the tester no longer calls known.

approvals.approved_version: known mark the tester made for those defects

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the tracker has no stable ids, the load is a one-time type and the mark stays. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Specify standards and procedures for release quality.

steps.what: Specify the quality standards for release readiness.
Draft procedures that quote only those standards.

loop.input: the standards the tester specified, each with an id
loop.output: procedures that cite only those ids
loop.check: every cited id must be one the tester specified; else discard
loop.stop: one draft; a standard with no check is left as a heading
loop.why_not_simpler: what the standard should be is not a procedure

steps.what: Determine which procedures define release quality.
File the standards and the chosen procedures.

tasks.design: The tester specifies the standards for release readiness. Procedures on {DOCS} may cite only those standards. The tester determines which procedures define quality. {PROJECT} files that set. A draft does not invent a standard.
tasks.previous_blocker: Release readiness was a meeting habit, different for each release.
tasks.enabler_now: A standard id is a field. What the standard should demand is not.
tasks.still_hard: How good is good enough for this product stays a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The tester knows which miss would be unacceptable in production.
tasks.altitude: Writing the procedures takes less time. Specifying the standards and determining release quality stay.

reach.task: Read the release standard before asking to ship

evidence.claim: A procedure that cites a specified standard can be checked. Setting the standard cannot.
Some products must show how release was decided. The source pack does not name a statute for this occupation, so the standard stays a signed file.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the tester specifies standards and procedures. Documenting a single test procedure for rerun is a different task. A release go-ahead on one change is also different.
Structured input: standard id, statement, procedure steps. Producer is the tester. A procedure citing an unknown id is discarded.
Specifying the standard is the large remaining share.
unknowns: Who else must sign a release standard?
research_questions: How often does release proceed with no written standard?

already_counted.description: Specifying the standards is already the remaining time on that step.

incremental.description: Retire standards the tester has withdrawn.

approvals.approved_version: procedures the tester determined for release quality

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If standards are not written down, the draft has nothing to cite and the tester still specifies them. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Monitor bug resolution efforts and track successes.

steps.what: Track resolution state of each open defect.
List successes and the defects still open.
Notify the developer of a stalled defect.

tasks.design: Resolution state and successes are a query on {PROJECT}, shown in {BI}. The tester monitors which efforts have stalled. A notice goes only for the stalled set the tester marked.
tasks.previous_blocker: Status was asked in a meeting, and a stuck defect waited until someone remembered it.
tasks.enabler_now: Open, fixed and retested are states a tracker can count. Whether an effort has stalled is not only a date.
tasks.still_hard: A defect that is quiet because it is hard, not forgotten, stays a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The tester knows which defect will miss the release if nobody moves it.

ambition.what: Look at stalled defects every day, not only at the release meeting.

tasks.altitude: Counting state takes less time. Deciding what has stalled stays, and it can happen daily.

reach.learn: Which defect the tester marked, and why

evidence.claim: A count of open and fixed defects is a query. Calling an effort stalled is not.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the tester monitors and notifies. The developer does the fix. Closing a defect is not this task.
Structured input: defect id, state, last change date, owner. Producer is the tracker. A defect with no id is not listed.
The monitor step is remaining time. The notice does not change the defect.
unknowns: Is there an owner and a last-change date on each defect?
What age counts as stuck before the tester looks?
research_questions: How many defects sit untouched until the release meeting?

already_counted.description: Monitoring stalled efforts is already the remaining time on that step.

incremental.description: Retire notices after the defect moves.

approvals.approved_version: stalled set the tester marked that day

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the tracker has no dates, the list is weak and the tester still monitors. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Update automated scripts so they stay current.

steps.what: Find automated scripts that fail on the new build.
Draft an update that changes only the failed step.

loop.input: the failed step id and the current script text
loop.output: an update that names that step and no other
loop.check: the update must name a step that failed; else discard
loop.stop: one draft; a failure with no step id is not updated
loop.why_not_simpler: whether the product changed, or only the script, is the review

steps.what: Review the update against the script's purpose.
Save the update to the automated scripts.

tasks.design: Failed automated scripts are listed from the run. A draft update may name only a step that failed. The tester reviews whether the product changed or only the script, then the update is saved. A failing script is not rewritten unattended.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scripts were patched in a hurry, and a real product bug was edited out of the check.
tasks.enabler_now: A failed step id is a field. Whether the assertion should change is not.
tasks.still_hard: Telling a product change from a brittle script stays a review.
tasks.human_edge: The tester knows what the script was meant to protect.
tasks.altitude: Finding the failed step takes less time. The review stays, so a script is not updated just to go green.

reach.task: See a script change beside the product change
reach.learn: Which step was updated, and why

evidence.claim: Listing failed scripts is a query. Changing an assertion so a bug disappears is a decision.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the tester updates scripts. Fixing the product is the developer's. Designing the original script is a different task.
Structured input: script id, step id, failure text, build. Producer is the run. An update that names no failed step is discarded.
Review time stays. Saving is not the review.
unknowns: Who else must accept a changed assertion?
research_questions: How often has a script been changed to hide a product bug?

already_counted.description: Reviewing the update is already the remaining time on that step.

incremental.description: Retire script versions that are no longer current.

approvals.approved_version: update the tester reviewed for that failed step

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If failures do not name a step, the draft is empty and the tester edits by hand. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The known-defect mark, the release standard and the stalled-bug judgement stay with the tester. Counts and loads shrink. A script update is saved only after a review, so a check is not edited away.
reach: Developers can query the known set.
A stalled defect is named on the day, not at the release meeting.
skills_to_grow: Refuse a script update that hides a product change.
Specify the standard before a procedure cites it.
role.ambitious_version: Stalled defects are looked at daily, and a release standard is a file rather than a habit.

job.title: Software Quality Assurance Analysts and Testers
